target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Scope SDK retry disable to embedded prompt lock path (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }` — the `0` is a **default** that goes before the caller options spread, so `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` (surfaced via `options.maxRetries` per the chain in `sdk.ts:360`) takes precedence when explicitly configured. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## Real behavior proof

> **Refreshed at current head `c21d0bc1a2` for the new timeout-retry exclusion (session write-lock timeouts excluded from the transient-timeout gate) and the restored organic-takeover real test. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: The transient-timeout retry restore (Fix #7) used `isTimeoutErrorMessage`, which also matches local `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` messages (`session file locked (timeout ...ms): ...`). That meant a local session write-lock coordination timeout was classified as a transient transport timeout and re-ran the whole model-fallback chain, even though retrying any model hits the same local condition. The timeout disjunct now excludes non-provider runtime coordination errors via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier — the same seam `model-fallback.ts` already uses to abort the chain on coordination errors. The connection/HTTP disjuncts are unchanged.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `c21d0bc1a2`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, deps installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps run after this patch**: Ran the affected suites at this head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <suite>`: the new session-write-lock-timeout exclusion regression in `agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, and the organic real-setup session-takeover regression (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence). The real-setup test depends on the `embedded-agent-helpers` mock exporting `isConnectionError`/`isTimeoutErrorMessage` (called eagerly on the catch path); those exports were missing, so this run also restores them so the test imports and runs to its assertion.
- **Observed result**: a session-write-lock-shaped timeout error now terminates as `run_failed` and is NOT re-run through the fallback chain (`runWithModelFallback` called exactly once); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance. The exclusion is proven non-tautological: removing the `!isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError(err)` clause makes the regression fail with the mock called twice.

### Real session-takeover path (organic error, real transport + real fence)

This proof drives the actual user-visible takeover path end to end and captures the real user-facing reply, rather than relying only on focused unit tests. Committed as `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-takeover.real.test.ts`.

**What is real (not hand-built):**
- A real on-disk session transcript file in a temp dir.
- A real local `node:http` server as the model `baseUrl` (`api: openai-completions`) that announces in-flight, then blocks before finishing the SSE body.
- The real `openai-completions` transport doing real HTTP I/O.
- The real embedded prompt-lock controller + fence (`createEmbeddedAttemptSessionLockController`), wired through the real `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` / `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` helpers — the exact helpers `attempt.ts` uses in production.
- The `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` is thrown **organically** by `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")` when a concurrent steering write changes the session-file fingerprint during the released-lock window — it is **not** constructed by hand.
- The real `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classification and the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch branch producing the user-facing payload.

**Mechanism (deterministic Promise handshakes, no sleeps):**
1. A real temp session file is created with one session line.
2. On the first model request the mock server resolves a `firstRequestReceived` deferred (the model call is in-flight), then blocks on a `releaseServer` deferred before writing the body.
3. `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` calls `releaseForPrompt()` at the start of the model call (opening the takeover window) and drains the real transport stream, so the released-lock window spans the real HTTP block.
4. While blocked, the test performs a concurrent "second user" steering write to the **same** real session file, changing its fingerprint.
5. `releaseServer` resolves; the server finishes the SSE body; the wrapped `finally{}` calls `reacquireAfterPrompt()` → `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")`.
6. The fingerprint mismatch trips the fence → `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` thrown organically → real classification → real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch.

The change at this seam converts the generic failure into specific resend guidance so the user knows their steering message must be resent.

Embedded prompt lock window injects `maxRetries: 0` but the native OpenAI transport never forwards it to the SDK, so SDK retries (default `maxRetries=2`) still occur during the released lock window, widening the race. Additionally, `queueMessage` steering writes bypass `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, causing fingerprint mismatch → `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` → generic failure branch → silent message loss.

target.title: fix(config): mark pre-update snapshot only after a successful write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` records the config path in a process-global "already snapshotted" set **before** it reads and writes the snapshot. If that first attempt fails transiently — a temporary file lock, an `EBUSY`, a momentary permission hiccup — the path is nonetheless marked done, so **no snapshot is ever taken for the rest of the process** and the operator silently loses their pre-update rollback point (#105193).

## Why This Change Was Made

The early mark was a guard against looping "on every later write". But `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` is only invoked once per `openclaw update` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts`), not on ordinary config writes — so the loop it guarded against does not occur, while the cost (dropping the snapshot on a transient first failure) is a real data-integrity gap.

The fix moves the `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten.add(...)` to **after** a successful write. On failure the path stays unmarked, so the next update attempt retries. Successful behavior is unchanged: the first successful call marks the path and later calls in the same process remain no-ops (the existing "once per process" and "survives multiple config writes" tests still pass).

## User Impact

- A transient failure on the first pre-update snapshot attempt no longer permanently disables snapshots; the operator keeps a rollback point on the next update.
- No behavior change on the success path or for the per-update (non-looping) call pattern.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` → 9/9): `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot retries after a transient first-attempt failure (#105193)` injects a `readFile` that throws `EBUSY` on the first call; it asserts no snapshot exists and the path is not marked, then a second call (read now succeeds) writes the `.pre-update` snapshot with the original content.

**Discriminator**: reverting only `backup-rotation.ts` (restoring mark-before-I/O) fails the new test — the second attempt is skipped because the path was marked on the failed first attempt, exactly the reported permanent block.

Fixes #105193

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP calls only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Gateway `/v1/embeddings` and capability-CLI paths call `embed` / `embedBatch` without a signal, so a server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers could hang the request forever. Memory/wiki callers already install their own deadlines; this gap is the unsignaled transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `signal` is omitted, pass `timeoutMs: 60_000` into the existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` hang bound (aligned with memory remote query defaults). When a caller already provides a signal, leave that deadline alone so memory search / tool timeouts are not clamped to 30–60s.

No new config surface. Test-only override shortens the floor for hang repros.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding requests (gateway HTTP embeddings, capability CLI) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Those requests fail with `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` after 60s. Callers that pass `AbortSignal` keep their own budget.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (`postEmbeddingRequest`)
- Production caller under test: `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider(...).provider.embed(...)` against a real local `node:http` server that never responds
- Regression: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- Sibling cases still green in the same file (UTF-16 error bounds, oversized JSON cancel, auth/config paths)

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |plugins| ... > times out embedding requests that never respond when caller omits signal 59ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > keeps caller AbortSignal deadlines instead of the no-signal transport floor 201ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.18s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding POSTs no longer hang forever when the upstream accepts the connection but never responds.
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway `embeddings-http` / capability CLI / direct provider → `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider` → `embed` / `embedBatch` → `postEmbeddingRequest` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` when `signal` is absent.
- **Boundary crossed:** Operator/remote OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP → local AbortSignal timeout via guarded fetch.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`. Does not override caller-owned signals used by memory-core `runEmbeddingOperationWithTimeout`. Does not add config/env.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node source checkout; production `provider.embed()` against real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` that reads the body and never writes a response.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts > openai-compatible generic embedding provider > keeps caller AbortSignal deadlines instead of the no-signal transport floor 201ms

 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts > openai-compatible generic embedding provider > bounds and cancels oversized successful embedding JSON bodies 42ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
   Duration  1.60s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.18s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** No-signal hang rejects with `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` within the shortened test floor (~50ms). Caller-provided `AbortSignal` is not clamped by that floor (still pending after 200ms until aborted). Existing embedding suites remain green.
- **What was not tested:** Live public embedding APIs; full gateway HTTP `/v1/embeddings` end-to-end against a hung upstream; memory-core batch paths (already signal-backed).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted
target.body:
Refs #104847

## Current Status

**Draft.** The current head is the single ACPX-focused commit `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `477f3af6883af1176fe88e9f8c561d6769097715`. Public exact-head macOS process, control-plane, abort-feedback, startup fail-closed, launchd service proof, and full CI pass. The previous current-head review reported one blocking P1 because the broad startup reaper dropped survivor evidence; this head propagates that evidence and adds the requested pending-lease regression. The PR remains Draft because technical review does not authorize the deliberate compatibility and availability policy; explicit ACPX/control-plane owner acceptance of the fail-closed contract is required.

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an ACP-backed turn could stop the visible reply while leaving an ACPX-owned worker alive after it detached from the wrapper's PPID tree. The existing reaper validated a wrapper process and walked its current parent/child tree, but `setsid`, double-fork, or later reparenting could move the autonomous worker outside that tree. The fast-abort path could also log cleanup failure and still report normal abort success.

## Root Cause

OpenClaw owned the outer ACPX runtime lifecycle but did not persist a process-ownership identity that survived PPID changes. Cancellation also treated cooperative ACP protocol cancellation as the lifecycle boundary, even though protocol cancel does not guarantee that detached host processes are gone.

The startup path had a second correctness gap: broad wrapper-root orphan cleanup called the survivor-aware termination helper but discarded `survivingPids`. A pending lease with `rootPid <= 0` could therefore be marked closed and allow ACPX registration even while an owned orphan remained alive.

## Code Path

1. `/stop` reaches the ACP manager cancellation path through `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts`.
2. `src/acp/control-plane/manager.cancel-session.ts` evicts the cached runtime handle and starts `close()` before best-effort protocol cancellation, so a rejected or never-settling protocol cancel cannot gate containment.
3. `extensions/acpx/src/runtime.ts` closes the ACPX turn owner and drains its process lease.
4. `extensions/acpx/src/process-reaper.ts` combines the live PPID tree with random lease and Gateway-instance markers, sends TERM, refreshes inventory, revalidates process identity before KILL, and performs a final survivor check.
5. `extensions/acpx/src/service.ts` drains stale open or pending leases before backend registration and now treats broad-reaper survivors as a startup failure.
6. Abort feedback reports containment failure instead of claiming success when cleanup cannot be verified.

## Behavior Changes

- ACP cancellation starts close and lease drain before best-effort protocol cancellation.
- Reparented descendants remain attributable by inherited random lease ID and Gateway instance ID.
- POSIX inventory uses bounded `ps eww` output only for in-memory matching and never logs process environments.
- Windows uses `Win32_Process` PID, PPID, command, and executable inventory; PPID-tree descendants use exact command and parent identity for delayed escalation.
- TERM-resistant targets are escalated only after fresh identity revalidation. A disappeared or reused PID is not signaled as the original target.
- Every targeted PID is included in final liveness verification even when TERM or KILL throws.
- Startup refuses ACPX registration when an open or pending lease cannot be verified or drained, including survivors returned by broad wrapper-root cleanup.
- Generic persistent `exec` and `process` background sessions are outside the ACPX lease path and keep their existing lifecycle.

## Compatibility And Migration

- No stored schema, config key, or user-data migration is introduced. Existing lease records keep the same shape.
- Cancellation now closes and evicts the reusable live ACP runtime handle; a later turn must reopen or resume instead of reusing that handle.
- Startup availability changes intentionally: an unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX lease blocks backend registration until containment succeeds or an operator resolves the stale process.
- There is no compatibility fallback in this patch. Maintainer acceptance of this fail-closed policy is required before Ready status.

## Evidence

### Before: launchd and process-group boundary

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof demonstrates that `launchctl bootout` removes the launchd leader and plain child while a `start_new_session` child and double-fork daemon survive:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352
- Baseline job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/job/86637125671
- Artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/artifacts/8258570570
- Artifact SHA-256: `b7a13f5f39f456ffc5070f427e522c1678098c71afd190b33d32e162e4d913b3`
- Evidence-only PR: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/pull/3

This is why launchd or process-group cleanup alone is not complete containment.

### After: exact-head candidate proof

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof checked out and verified `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352
- Candidate job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/job/86637125683
- Artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/artifacts/8258578919
- Artifact SHA-256: `4eb6a4389962505d62141adc0da2c326cef09426e3e7f5135cf80a1f939e4a72`
- ACPX process/runtime/service suites: 4 files, 104 tests passed.
- ACP manager cancellation: 1 file, 4 tests passed.
- Abort and operator feedback: 1 file, 33 tests passed.
- The new regressions prove broad startup survivor propagation and startup refusal for a `rootPid: 0` pending lease whose owned orphan remains alive.

### Service-managed ownership proof

The same exact-head job runs the production lease and reaper implementation under a launchd-managed service:

- Before abort: service alive, lease-owned reparented descendant alive, unrelated persistent background alive.
- After abort: service alive, lease-owned descendant gone, unrelated persistent background alive.
- Cleanup inspected and terminated the leased PID and reported no survivors.
- Every evidence pipeline uses `set -o pipefail`, so harness failure cannot be hidden by `tee`.

### Full CI

- Exact-head full CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187865437
- Status: passed for exact head `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`; all selected jobs completed successfully.
- Upstream PR checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104929/checks
- Local lightweight preflight: targeted `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed. Builds, type checks, lint, and test suites run in GitHub Actions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- Real POSIX detached and reparented lease cleanup.
- Lease environment matching with Gateway-instance isolation.
- TERM-resistant escalation, signal failures, final survivor verification, and PID-reuse identity revalidation.
- Windows process inventory and delayed PPID-tree escalation identity.
- Broad startup reaper survivor propagation.
- Pending lease with `rootPid <= 0` blocks startup when an owned orphan survives.
- Runtime close failure marks containment lost and propagates failure.
- Cancellation starts close and lease drain before rejected or never-settling protocol cancel.
- `/stop` returns containment failure instead of false success.

## Performance

- Process inventory runs only during ACPX cancellation and startup stale-lease recovery, not on the steady-state turn path.
- POSIX process output is bounded to 8 MiB.
- Cleanup deduplicates target PIDs and reuses one broad-root result for pending leases sharing a wrapper root.

## Risk And Rollback

- The deliberate compatibility risk is loss of live-handle reuse after cancellation.
- The deliberate availability risk is startup refusal when stale ACPX containment cannot be proven.
- Process ownership matching is security-sensitive; PID reuse is handled by fresh identity checks before escalation and by final inventory verification.
- Reverting the commit restores cooperative cancel reuse, PPID-only cleanup, and the previous startup behavior.

## Maintainer Decision Required

Should OpenClaw intentionally override upstream ACPX cooperative-cancel semantics by closing and evicting the reusable runtime handle, and should any unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX lease block backend startup?

Recommended policy: accept the fail-closed contract because the alternative can report a turn stopped while an autonomous credentialed worker remains alive. This PR will stay Draft until the relevant ACPX/runtime owner explicitly accepts that compatibility and availability tradeoff.

## Not Tested

- No private Claude credentials or paid-provider runtime were used.
- Public CI uses deterministic real host processes plus the production ACPX lease, reaper, control-plane, and abort-feedback implementations.

target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation in terminal output, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface to a human reader as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses human-facing array-index path formatting for config validation diagnostics; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a documented machine-readable dot path and is serialized through `openclaw config validate --json`. The reviewer correctly pointed out that changing that shared field to bracket notation would be a compatibility break for scripts and sibling consumers.

This revision keeps the shared validation path contract unchanged and moves bracket notation to the terminal issue-formatting boundary only. JSON output and normalized/shared validation issues continue to use dot paths such as `agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting`.

## User Impact

Users reading non-JSON config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

Machine-readable consumers keep the existing representation:

```json
{
  "path": "agents.list.3.tools.profile",
  "message": "Invalid input"
}
```

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both display and contract behavior:

```ts
formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
  { pathStyle: "display" },
) -> "- agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"

formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
) -> "- agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"
```

The CLI regression test also checks both surfaces:

```text
openclaw config validate        -> agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting
openclaw config validate --json -> agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting
```

Validation run locally on the review-fix revision:

```powershell
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --reporter verbose
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --testNamePattern "path|config validate|numeric path|JSON" --reporter verbose
git diff --check
```

Results:

- formatter + validation focused run: `2 passed`, `41 tests passed`
- CLI focused run covering `config validate` and `--json`: `1 passed`, `49 tests passed`, `81 skipped`
- `git diff --check`: passed

A previously attempted focused `config-misc` single-test run timed out inside the existing async snapshot test body after 120s. The touched assertion in that file is only the expected path string (`agents.list[0].sandbox` -> `agents.list.0.sandbox`), and the narrower validation/CLI tests above cover the requested contract directly.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config validation failure
  -> Zod issue path array
  -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()
  -> ConfigValidationIssue.path remains dot-path
  -> config validate --json serializes the dot-path issue unchanged
  -> non-JSON config validate output calls formatConfigIssueLines(..., { pathStyle: "display" })
  -> terminal diagnostics render numeric dot segments as bracket indices
```

Affected surface is limited to human-facing `config validate` issue rendering for numeric path segments. This PR intentionally leaves shared validation issue objects, JSON output, config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, source line-number lookup, and bad-value rendering unchanged.

Related: #104854

target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

![Composer with image and pasted text attachments](https://calm-mill-vpd8.here.now/pasted-text-with-image.png)

![Composer with pasted text attachment only](https://calm-mill-vpd8.here.now/pasted-text-only.png)

This changes the Control UI composer so plain-text pastes over 1000 characters become compact `text/plain` attachments instead of filling the textarea.

The attachment uses the existing chat attachment payload path. - Converts long plain-text paste events into `pasted-text-*.txt` composer attachments.
- Shows a compact attachment card with a short preview from the pasted text.
- Keeps the default composer placeholder for pasted-text-only attachments.

- Preserves the existing attachment send path for retry, queueing, cleanup, and payload serialization.

target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation in terminal output, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface to a human reader as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses human-facing array-index path formatting for config validation diagnostics; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a documented machine-readable dot path and is serialized through `openclaw config validate --json`. The reviewer correctly pointed out that changing that shared field to bracket notation would be a compatibility break for scripts and sibling consumers.

This revision keeps the shared validation path contract unchanged and moves bracket notation to the terminal issue-formatting boundary only. JSON output and normalized/shared validation issues continue to use dot paths such as `agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting`.

## User Impact

Users reading non-JSON config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

Machine-readable consumers keep the existing representation:

```json
{
  "path": "agents.list.3.tools.profile",
  "message": "Invalid input"
}
```

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both display and contract behavior:

```ts
formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
  { pathStyle: "display" },
) -> "- agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"

formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
) -> "- agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"
```

The CLI regression test also checks both surfaces:

```text
openclaw config validate        -> agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting
openclaw config validate --json -> agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting
```

Validation run locally on the review-fix revision:

```powershell
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --reporter verbose
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --testNamePattern "path|config validate|numeric path|JSON" --reporter verbose
git diff --check
```

Results:

- formatter + validation focused run: `2 passed`, `41 tests passed`
- CLI focused run covering `config validate` and `--json`: `1 passed`, `49 tests passed`, `81 skipped`
- `git diff --check`: passed

A previously attempted focused `config-misc` single-test run timed out inside the existing async snapshot test body after 120s. The touched assertion in that file is only the expected path string (`agents.list[0].sandbox` -> `agents.list.0.sandbox`), and the narrower validation/CLI tests above cover the requested contract directly.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config validation failure
  -> Zod issue path array
  -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()
  -> ConfigValidationIssue.path remains dot-path
  -> config validate --json serializes the dot-path issue unchanged
  -> non-JSON config validate output calls formatConfigIssueLines(..., { pathStyle: "display" })
  -> terminal diagnostics render numeric dot segments as bracket indices
```

Affected surface is limited to human-facing `config validate` issue rendering for numeric path segments. This PR intentionally leaves shared validation issue objects, JSON output, config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, source line-number lookup, and bad-value rendering unchanged.

Related: #104854

target.title: fix(retry): avoid status code substring matches
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users encountering permanent provider errors or multi-hour rate limits would have the session retry up to three times, re-sending the same context even though the error cannot clear within the retry window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retryable HTTP status codes now match only standalone status tokens, so model identifiers, image dimensions, and API keys cannot accidentally trigger retries. The classifier also recognizes daily limits and hour/day retry windows as non-retryable, while preserving normal transient 429 and 5xx handling.

## User Impact

Sessions now stop promptly for permanent provider failures and long-lived quotas instead of making additional doomed calls. Transient provider and network failures keep their existing retry behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts` — 11 passing.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — no actionable findings.
- Attempted required Testbox pre-warm, but the configured Crabbox wrapper could not pass its local binary sanity check; therefore this PR has focused local fallback proof and pending GitHub CI rather than Testbox proof.

AI-assisted; the diff and tests were reviewed before submission.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling an agent run while a Kimi (Moonshot) `web_search` request was pending would leave that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reached the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discarded the execution context, so the request could remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The Kimi tool accepted only `args` and dropped the tool execution context — `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` had no `opts` parameter and `createTool` ignored `context`. The downstream `runKimiSearch` already accepted a `signal` field but the caller never passed one in, so the signal died at the provider boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix across the existing cancellation boundaries: the Kimi tool now accepts the execution context and passes its `AbortSignal` through `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`.

The change does not alter Kimi configuration, schemas, cache keys, timeouts, SSRF policy, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks the signal handoff and proves that reverting the fix causes test failure.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` accepts context |
| Signal pass | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 66 | `{ signal: context?.signal }` |
| Tool exec | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 349 | `opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }` |
| Run search | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 401 | `signal: opts?.signal` |
| Search client | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 234 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal: params.signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` |
| Timeout | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` |
| Native | `fetch()` | — | Native `AbortSignal` support |

### Real behavior proof — pre-aborted signal through full provider chain

```
[proof] Pre-aborted signal propagated through Kimi provider in 1293ms
[proof] error: Error: proof: pre-aborted signal
```

- Signal flows from provider.execute() through all intermediate layers to fetch()
- buildTimeoutAbortSignal sees pre-aborted parent signal → immediately aborts controller
- No network I/O occurs (fake API key passes the credential check)
- false-positive regression guard: if execute resolves (signal forwarding reverted) → test fails

### Real behavior proof — in-flight cancel through real Kimi API

When `KIMI_API_KEY` is set, the test dispatches a real query and aborts mid-flight at ~500ms:

```json
{
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledMs": <N>,
  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "proof: in-flight cancellation",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "signalGuard": "provider.execute → runKimiSearch → withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint → fetch()"
}
```

### Real behavior proof — stalled-server through guarded-fetch stack

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 110ms through guarded-fetch stack
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
```

(withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint shares identical fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch() path)

### Regression test — signal reaches fetch (control-red verifiable)

The unit test creates a fetch mock that rejects when the passed signal fires. The test:
1. Starts a search with an `AbortController`
2. Waits for fetch() to be called
3. Aborts the controller mid-flight
4. Asserts the search rejects
5. Asserts the signal passed to fetch is defined and aborted

**Control-red**: reverting `signal: context?.signal` from the provider → fetch is called without a signal → `fetchSignal` stays undefined → test fails. This was NOT true in R2 where the test only checked `fetchMock.toHaveBeenCalled()` (passes even with reverted fix).

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 19/19 passed (2 test files)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
✓ clean (exit 0)
```

### tsgo

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
✓ exit 0, no errors
```

### Control-red

| Version | Behavior | Test result |
|---------|----------|------------|
| **PR (R3)** | Signal reaches fetch → abort propagates | ✅ passes |
| **Revert signal forwarding** | `execute(ctx, args)` drops context → fetch called without signal | ❌ FAILS: fetchSignal is undefined |

Revert diff (the exact lines removed to test):
```diff
- execute: async (args, context) => {
-   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args, { signal: context?.signal });
+ execute: async (args) => {
+   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args);
```

### Pre-push checklist

| Gate | Check | Result |
|------|-------|--------|
| G1 | `git diff --stat origin/main` | 4 files, +256/-2 |
| G2 | `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` | 1 commit |
| G3 | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/...` | 19/19 passed |
| G4 | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (4 files) | clean (exit 0) |
| G5 | `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` | clean (exit 0) |
| G6 | `git diff --check origin/main` | clean |
| G7 | `git status --porcelain` | 4 M files only |

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor memory_search deadline during wiki exhaustive scan
target.body:
Closes #104719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"` or `corpus="all"` against a large compiled-wiki vault would hit `memory_search timed out after 15s` when digest-selected candidates underfilled `maxResults`. The wiki supplement then continued a full remaining-vault Markdown scan after the tool had already timed out, so agents lost wiki recall and the host kept doing orphan I/O.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory tool already owns a fixed deadline (`AbortSignal`), but the corpus-supplement bridge never forwarded it into memory-wiki search. Exhaustive underfill scanning then read remaining pages with no cancellation points.

This PR threads an optional `signal` through `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` → wiki corpus supplement → `searchMemoryWiki` / `searchWikiCorpus`, and makes page reads batch-aware so an aborted deadline returns partial results and stops further file I/O.

Unlike approaches that permanently disable exhaustive backfill for supplements (which need a feature-owner completeness tradeoff), exhaustive recall remains the default when the search is still within budget. Direct `wiki_search` is unchanged except that it can also honor an optional signal if a caller provides one.

## User Impact

Agents using compiled-wiki supplements through `memory_search` no longer leave large orphan vault scans running after a tool timeout. On-budget multi-result wiki recall still gets exhaustive underfill when needed. Operators avoid multi-second post-timeout host work on large vaults.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (agent review follow-up)

Lint (exact CS finding):
- Fixed `oxc(no-map-spread)` at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` page-read map:
  `{ ...summary, raw }` → `Object.assign({}, summary, { raw })` (same shape, no map spread).
- Focused oxlint on the file: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` on `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts`.

Focused tests (all pass after fix):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  4 passed | 41 skipped (45)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/corpus-supplement.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.
- Oxlint passed for all nine changed files.
